name: Honolulu
operatingHours: Skyline rail runs daily ~4:00 AM–10:30 PM, every ~10 min, on its 13 open stations from East Kapolei to Kahauiki (Middle Street–Kalihi Transit Center) via the airport and Pearl Harbor. It does not yet reach Downtown, Ala Moana or Waikiki (Civic Center extension due ~2031); TheBus covers those, some routes 24 hours.
fareInfo: Skyline and TheBus share fares: $3 adult per ride on a HOLO card (card $2) with free transfers for 2.5 hours; fares cap at $7.50/day and $80/month (2026). Tap the HOLO card at the station gate before boarding.

lines.name: Skyline
stations: University of Hawaiʻi at West Oʻahu

hotels.name: Embassy Suites by Hilton Waikiki Beach Walk

sights.name: Diamond Head State Monument
sights.note: An extinct volcanic crater whose steep summit trail ends at old military bunkers with a sweeping view over Waikiki.
sights.hours: Daily 6 AM–6 PM (last entry ~4:30 PM); timed entry + parking reservation required for non-residents

sights.name: Pearl Harbor National Memorial
sights.note: The National Park Service visitor centre and museums telling the story of the 7 December 1941 attack.

sights.name: USS Arizona Memorial
sights.note: A white memorial straddling the sunken battleship, reached by Navy shuttle boat after a short film at the visitor centre.
sights.hours: Programs daily ~8 AM–3:30 PM every ~15 min; boats may be cancelled in high wind

sights.name: ʻIolani Palace
sights.note: The restored 1880s home of Hawaii's last monarchs, the only royal palace on US soil.

sights.name: Waikiki Beach
sights.note: Honolulu's famous hotel-lined crescent of sand, good for gentle surf lessons and sunset views of Diamond Head.

sights.name: Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve
sights.note: A sheltered volcanic-crater bay with a coral reef, Oahu's best-known snorkelling spot (about 25 min east of Waikiki).
sights.hours: Wed–Sun ~6:45 AM–4 PM; closed Mon–Tue; online reservation required; temporary closures for sewer works expected into 2027

sights.name: Manoa Falls
sights.note: A muddy rainforest walk at the head of Manoa Valley to a tall, thin waterfall (pin at trailhead; falls ~1.3 km up).
sights.hours: Trail daily dawn–dusk; paid parking at trailhead

sights.name: Bishop Museum
sights.note: Hawaii's state museum of natural and cultural history, with royal heirlooms in the grand Hawaiian Hall and a planetarium.

sights.name: Battleship Missouri Memorial
sights.note: The battleship on whose deck Japan's WWII surrender was signed, moored on Ford Island near the Arizona.
sights.hours: Daily ~8 AM–4 PM; shuttle from Pearl Harbor visitor center

sights.name: Aloha Stadium Swap Meet & Marketplace
sights.note: A big open-air flea market of souvenirs, aloha shirts and snacks, now in the stadium's lower parking lot near Hālawa Skyline station.
sights.hours: Wed & Sat 8 AM–3 PM, Sun 6:30 AM–3 PM; $2 entry (cash)

sights.name: U.S. Army Museum of Hawaii
sights.note: A free military history museum inside a 1911 coastal artillery battery at Fort DeRussy, steps from the beach.

sights.name: Ala Moana Beach Park
sights.note: A long, calm, reef-protected beach park popular with local families, with lawns and picnic spots opposite Ala Moana Center.

sights.name: Pearl Harbor Aviation Museum
sights.note: Historic WWII hangars on Ford Island displaying warplanes, with bullet holes from the 1941 attack still in the windows.
sights.hours: Daily ~8 AM–4 PM; shuttle from Pearl Harbor visitor center

sights.name: USS Bowfin Submarine Museum & Park
sights.note: A WWII submarine you can climb through, plus a museum of undersea warfare beside the Pearl Harbor visitor centre.

sights.name: National Memorial Cemetery of the Pacific
sights.note: A military cemetery set inside Punchbowl Crater, with a memorial and lookout over downtown.
sights.hours: Daily 8 AM–5:30 PM (to 6:30 PM Mar–Sep); free

sights.name: Honolulu Museum of Art
sights.note: Hawaii's largest art museum, with Asian, Pacific and Western collections around peaceful courtyards; Shangri La tours leave from here.
sights.hours: Wed–Sun ~10 AM–6 PM (to 9 PM Fri–Sat); closed Mon–Tue

sights.name: Magic Island
sights.note: A man-made peninsula with a calm lagoon and a free sunset spot looking back along the Waikiki skyline.

sights.name: Saturday Farmers' Market KCC
sights.note: A lively Saturday-morning market of local produce and island food stalls on the Kapiʻolani Community College campus below Diamond Head.

airports.name: Daniel K. Inouye International Airport
airports.transitNote: Skyline's Lelepaua (Airport) station, on this map, sits by Terminal 2 and links via a walkway from the terminal parking garage, but rail doesn't reach Waikiki: take the W Line bus (TheBus, limited-stop, ~45–60 min, $3 HOLO; luggage must fit on your lap or under the seat) or a taxi/rideshare (~$45–60, 25–40 min).
airports.hours: Skyline: first train ~4:00 AM, last ~10:30 PM
